<description>
Picks up #28538

Outbound-full-relay slots should be used by peers that actually relay transactions, besides #28538 see #16418 and #28371 for the motivation. So try to replace peers that are not relaying txs with peers that do.

The approach differs from the original PR in a few details in response to some of the review comments there:

- A replacement is connected before the peer is evicted. The original PR disconnected a non-tx-relaying peer once all full outbound slots were filled. Reviewers preferred having a replacement available first (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28538#issuecomment-1883481846). Now an extra outbound-full-relay connection is requested, like the extra network-specific peers, and the existing eviction of extra outbound peers prefers peers that don't relay txs.
- Peers not relaying txs don't get `m_protect`. Otherwise they could stay forever (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28538#discussion_r1443336121), and ignoring the protection was rejected in the same thread (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28538#discussion_r1443312604).
- An only peer on a network is not replaced. Otherwise the network-specific extra connections and this logic would keep replacing each other (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28538#issuecomment-1883481846). This also covers the `-maxconnections=1` case (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28538#discussion_r1417178196).

Nothing is changed in `-blocksonly` mode or during IBD. The rename commit and the functional test are taken from the original PR with some changes to match the new behavior.
</description>

[2026-11-18] c:6985315949 comment by fjahr (member):
Addressed code review from @fametrano and @Bicaru20, thanks! I took the suggested test changes mostly with a few edits. Aside from addressing the comments I also expanded the tests with additional checks in a few places.

[quoted text omitted]
@Bicaru20 Good question. The last block announcement only decides between peers of the same kind. A tx relaying peer that stays silent is still handled by the chain sync and stale tip logic, and we have the block-relay-only peers on top of that.

[quoted text omitted]
@instagibbs The replacement peer makes the same claims as every other full outbound peer we connect to while the evicted peer has told us that it will drop our transactions. So I don't think we can end up doing worse in terms of tx relay and the four block relay peers are protected anyway.

If that still seems undesirable I could see two possible tweaks to the concept: 1. we could only evict once the replacement has sent us a transaction, but of course that is easy to do for an attacker that is lying to us. Or 2. we could tolerate one or two blocksonly peers and only replace the ones beyond that threshold, which was already mentioned as an option in #28538. I prefer the current approach and I don't think there are any harmful effects but I am open to adopt if reviewers prefer a different change.

[quoted text omitted]
For a more complete answer I will try to do a fresh crawl of the network since I didn't find a recent dataset that included the flags. But the [KIT monitoring snapshots](https://www.dsn.kastel.kit.edu/bitcoin/data.html) record block and tx announcements per reachable peer which should be a good approximation with the caveat that it only covers IPv4 and IPv6. Over the last year somewhere between 1% and 2% of the peers there announced blocks but no transactions, with a slight upward trend. That's about 100 to 150 nodes, not sure how inflated their total node counts may be from sybils etc. But anyway it indeed does not seem to be a big problem today and I see it more as a cheap precaution. Had the BIP110 campaign aimed at making node runners deactivate their mempool for example, this could have been relevant.

| Network | Handshakes | `relay=0` | Share | P(≥1 of 8 full outbound peers) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 5,618 | 85 | 1.51% | 11.5% |
| IPv6 | 549 | 11 | 2.00% | 15.0% |
| Tor | 10,277 | 58 | 0.56% | 4.4% |
| I2P | 4,671 | 12 | 0.26% | 2.0% |
| All | 21,115 | 166 | 0.79% | 6.1% |

So the share on Tor is even smaller than on clearnet and the KIT data matches the result closely.
